t:
That title 10 of the United States Code is hereby amended as follows:
Subsection 2306(f) is amended by adding the following paragraph:

“For the purpose of evaluating the accuracy, completeness, and currency of cost or pricing data required to be submitted by this subsection, any authorized representative of the head of the agency who is an employee of the United States Government shall have the right, until the expiration of three years after final payment under the contract or subcontract, to examine all books, records, documents, and other data, of the contractor or subcontractor related to the negotiation, pricing, or performance of the contract or subcontract.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that contractors and subcontractors, who are outside parties, are involved with a federal agency. But the provision only gives federal employees the right to audit contractor records to verify cost or pricing data. That is an oversight and enforcement power, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision, and it creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: any authorized representative of the head of the agency who is an employee of the United States Government shall have the right, until the expiration of three years after final payment under the contract or subcontract, to examine all books, records, documents, and other data, of the contractor or subcontractor

opus.w: This provision lets federal employees audit a contractor's records to check the accuracy of cost or pricing data. The government acts on the contractor here; it does not ask outside parties for input before a federal decision. A private contractor is mentioned, but it has no role in shaping the decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: any authorized representative of the head of the agency who is an employee of the United States Government shall have the right, until the expiration of three years after final payment under the contract or subcontract, to examine all books, records, documents, and other data, of the contractor or subcontractor
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading:** A private party (the contractor or subcontractor) deals with a federal agency here, so this could look like an outsider taking part. It doesn't fit the definition. The provision only gives a federal employee the right to examine the contractor's records to check cost or pricing data. That is an audit or enforcement power. The government is not consulting anyone, holding a hearing, taking comments, creating an advisory body or giving anyone a right to sue before it makes a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants federal employees the right to audit contractor records. It does not require the government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from outside parties before making a decision. The interaction is one-sided oversight, not participatory decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: any authorized representative of the head of the agency who is an employee of the United States Government shall have the right... to examine all books, records, documents, and other data, of the contractor or subcontractor
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing government representatives to examine contractor records constitutes "participation" because it involves interaction with outside entities (contractors). However, this is an audit/inspection power granted to the government, not a requirement for the government to consult with or coordinate with outsiders before making a decision. The contractors are not participating in the decision-making process; they are subject to oversight.
